title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2610.29504v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) perform unevenly across forecasting tasks. Recent work uses agentic model orchestration (AMO) to select or combine TSFMs, often outperforming individual forecasters. Yet these gains may reflect stronger or more complementary candidates rather than better orchestration. To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. Experiments on GIFT-Eval show that AMO improves accuracy, but its gains are bounded by the candidate TSFMs. The best orchestrators reduce MASE by less than 6% relative to the best single TSFM across all tasks. These gains depend on complementarity (different candidates excel on different tasks) rather than the number of candidates. translated_title: 重新思考用于时间序列预测的智能体模型编排
translated_abstract: 时间序列基础模型（TSFMs）在不同预测任务上的表现参差不齐。近期研究采用智能体模型编排（AMO）来选择或组合TSFMs，其效果往往优于单个预测器。然而，这些收益可能源于更强或更具互补性的候选模型，而非更好的编排本身。为了厘清这两种效应，我们提出了FairAMO，一种采用冻结候选预测的受控评估协议。在GIFT-Eval上的实验表明，AMO确实能提升预测准确性，但其收益受限于候选TSFMs的上限：在所有任务中，最佳编排器相对于最佳单个TSFM的MASE降低幅度不到6%。这些收益取决于模型间的互补性（即不同候选模型在不同任务上各有所长），而非候选模型的数量。增加成员会带来边际收益递减，而一个冗余成员甚至可能抵消全部收益。此外，历史证据的价值也很快达到饱和——仅需几个近期时间窗口即可捕获全部收益。
tldr: 该论文提出FairAMO受控评估协议，揭示智能体模型编排（AMO）在时间序列预测中的收益本质上受限于候选基础模型本身，其关键在于模型互补性而非数量，且相对最佳单一模型的MASE改进不足6%。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol revealing that the gains of agentic model orchestration (AMO) in time series forecasting are fundamentally bounded by candidate foundation models, driven by complementarity rather than candidate count, and yield less than 6% MASE improvement over the best single model.
